text:
jordyn: heads-up — noticed a 30-40ms p99 jump on prod after yesterday's kernel-autotune merge. looks related to kernel path switches under continuous-batching pressure. logs attached in the incident (brief below).

mike: saw that too on staging around the same time. p50 fine, p99 pulls out. seems correlated with bursts that have mixed seq lengths.

sana: any chance it's kv-cache cold starts? if KV miss rate spikes we end up forcing kernel handoff for warmup which adds launch overhead + extra kernel switches.

jordyn: perf-bot pulled some metrics: 
perf-bot: GPU kernel-switch-rate: +3.4x, launch-latency-tail +22ms, continuous-batch-fill-time slightly higher. KV hit-rate dip ~8% at spike.

mike: interesting — our kernel-selector recently started preferring arch-optimized kernels for short sequences but will switch for >512 tokens. if a burst mixes 64/1024 it can flip back and forth. sticky-path hysteresis might help.

sana: agree. proposal: add a hysteresis window to kernel-selector so it only switches if consecutive N requests exceed threshold. also consider delaying KV cache eviction so warmups don't coincide with autoscale bursts.

jordyn: quick repro I ran (local):
```
# reproduce mixed shapes
ab-bench --rps 200 --shapes "64x8,1024x1" --duration 60s --client=sim
```
That produced the same p99 bump locally and we captured a flame sample.

jordyn: flame excerpt:
```
sample  45%  kernel_selector::choose_path
sample  20%  runtime::launch_kernel
sample  15%  kv_cache::populate
sample  10%  scheduler::continuous_batch
```

mike: that lines up. I can push a quick config change to add a 3-request hysteresis + prefer current kernel for 200ms before switching. low-risk canary.

ci-deploy-bot: deploy 2078769460 by ryan: branch=autotune-safe-hysteresis, env=canary

ryan: rolled canary at 2078769460. monitoring now.

perf-bot: canary metrics (first 2m): p99 down ~18ms vs baseline, kernel-switch-rate -55% on canary hosts, KV hit-rate stable.

jordyn: nice. action items: (1) mike to iterate hysteresis into selector code and add unit tests; (2) sana to validate KV eviction TTLs and add a short-term bump; (3) jordyn to run long soak with mixed-shape load and capture e2e traces. I'll open a perf ticket and tag eng-runtime.

mike: I'll open PR with config and perf tests, link reproducer and flamegraphs.

sana: I'll check cache TTLs and put a small experiment behind a flag. if stable, propose default bump.

jordyn: thanks — marking this resolved for now but keeping watch for end-of-day. :thumbsup:
